task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 17, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer about the service charge at the Copper Wren restaurant, answering where the charge goes and how it differs from an optional tip under this business's stated policy.

facts.text: Copper Wren introduced an 18% service charge on dine-in food and drink checks in July 2026.
A $50 eligible check receives a $9 service charge, making $59 before separately calculated taxes.
The charge does not apply to takeaway orders under the restaurant's policy.
The restaurant retains the service-charge receipts as business revenue used for payroll, paid leave and other labor costs.
It does not promise to hand the full 18% from each table directly to that table's server.
The restaurant raised servers' base pay from $16 to $22 an hour when the charge began.
The higher base rate is not a guarantee of a fixed number of shifts or a particular weekly take-home amount.
Customers may leave an additional optional tip, but the payment screen starts with no additional tip selected.
The restaurant's notice asks diners not to treat the service charge as an automatic obligation to add another 18%.
Owner Leda Selt says the policy is intended to make the base wage less dependent on the size of individual table tips.
Selt said, "We can promise an hourly rate more clearly than we can promise what a particular table will leave."
Server Toma Dain says the new base rate makes quiet shifts easier to plan around, while busy nights previously could produce larger tips.
Dain said, "A steadier floor matters, but people should not assume every worker's total went up by the same amount."
The reporting record lacks matched shift-by-shift earnings data establishing every employee's total change.
Kitchen workers also receive pay under the revised labor budget, but their individual rates are not provided.
The service charge appears on menus and the restaurant's booking page; it is not introduced only on the final receipt.
Menu base prices were unchanged at the July transition, so customers' mandatory pretax totals increased for eligible dine-in orders.
The restaurant has not published a verified profit comparison before and after the change.
Copper Wren has 46 seats and serves lunch and dinner five days a week.
This account describes one restaurant's allocation policy, not a universal legal rule governing all service charges or tips.
